About Me

Strategist. Consultant.
Educator. Changemaker.

Currently serving as Principal Consultant at AIVidya, I help organizations design transformation and growth strategies powered by Artificial Intelligence. I work with corporates and students to build AI-ready leadership frameworks that deliver measurable outcomes.

My career spans over two decades across IBM, Dell Technologies, Surya Roshni, 3i Infotech, Vertex, and World Intellectual Foundation — where I have led cross-functional teams, driven ERP transformations, and shaped public policy research.

I began my career as a Systems Engineer at Tata Steel after graduating from IIT Varanasi, and later completed my MBA from IIM Bangalore specializing in Strategy and Information Systems. I am deeply passionate about mentoring the next generation of leaders and contributing to informed public discourse through writing.

Artificial Intelligence

Will Artificial Intelligence Take Away Livelihoods?

Usage of Artificial Intelligence is becoming more enhanced everyday with software engineers round the globe contributing to its robustness through open source platforms. It has been extensively used by product marketing companies to study consumer behavior patterns for designing schemes and promotions accordingly.

Many people have a misconception that AI will make their jobs redundant. This is similar to the fear that people had when ERP packages like SAP, Oracle etc. were implemented. However, instead of replacing jobs, ERP implementations created opportunities for employees in support functions to be redeployed in more productive areas. Same is the foreseeable future of AI.

Let's start by examining the difference between Artificial Intelligence and Human Intelligence. Both are based on large repositories of data stored in a memory bank. Experts estimate the capacity of human brain to be at most 2.5 petabytes, which is way smaller than what AI machines can store. However, where the human brain proves superior is in drawing inferences using instinct, gut feel, and common sense — the very thing AI cannot replicate.

Industry Impact at a Glance

Across sectors from healthcare to education and financial services, AI will play an enabling rather than replacing role. Dr Atul Gawande summarized it well: "AI will not replace doctors, but a doctor who does not know how to use AI will be replaced by one who does."

Key Hindrances

  • Building a vast repository of data for patterns analysis and machine learning
  • Availability of 5G/6G capacity networks connected over cloud in real time
  • Confidential consumer data sharing — a global data protection policy is urgently needed

For AI to stand on its own feet, competing entities will need to share restricted data with each other, after having taken consent from their customers. That remains the defining challenge of our era.

Technology & Society

The Emotional Tipping Point of AI

I feel that if you ever start feeling emotionally attached to Artificial Intelligence, is when all the worst fears of the critics of AI will come true. Because AI will then bypass the EQ of humans.

Our dependence on Broad and Generative AI will make us lose our confidence in our instincts, intuitions and sixth sense — where so far the neural network of human brains have been able to outperform human coded software.

People "will" lose jobs, there will be ethical violations and loss of control on daily lives. Next time you read a disclaimer that "XXX" is AI and can make mistakes, take it seriously.

And when on a prompt line, you reply "Thanks" to an AI software, you are better off watching AI created web series — because that's what AI will start with. Supervised teaching.

AI Governance

Governance and Ethics in AI

Today everyone is talking about the wonders of Artificial Intelligence. What it is doing now, and what it can do in future. Narrow, Broad, General. Supervised, Unsupervised and Reinforced Learning. These fundamentals of AI are commonplace jargon. Prompt engineering is used by almost every human as inputs to lead to intricate and calculated outcomes, which were previously not possible. And the world has gone crazy over Generative AI.

However, there are a couple of areas of AI which will surely gain prominence in the near future, as they are being neglected by most startups and even stalwarts — because of lack of clear cut international policy frameworks and guidelines. These are "governance" and "ethics".

Even though everyone talks about it, nobody cares to listen or take it seriously enough. This issue may become a show stopper for many boutique firms.

And this is just the beginning…

Fintech

How AI Is Rewiring Fintech from Inside Out: The Silent Revolution

AI isn't coming to Fintech. It is already here, and it's changing everything.

From fraud detection that flags suspicious transactions in milliseconds, to credit scoring models that assess risk more fairly and accurately than traditional methods. AI is making financial services smarter, faster, and more inclusive.

Robo-advisors are democratising wealth management, putting personalised investment strategies in the hands of everyday users. Chatbots and virtual assistants are resolving customer queries 24/7 with human-like precision, cutting costs while improving customer experience.

In capital markets, milliseconds matter and data volumes are staggering. AI is the only tool operating at the speed and scale the market demands. Algorithmic trading systems now execute complex strategies in microseconds by reading order books, sentiment signals, and macro data simultaneously.

AI is transforming risk management, stress-testing portfolios against thousands of market scenarios in real time, flagging tail risks before they cascade. Surveillance and compliance are being revolutionised too — AI monitors millions of transactions simultaneously, detecting market manipulation and insider trading patterns that rule-based systems consistently miss.

Perhaps most powerfully, AI is opening doors for the unbanked. By analysing alternative data like mobile usage and transaction patterns, lenders can now serve billions who were previously invisible to the financial system.

The winners in Fintech won't just be those who adopt AI. They'll be those who deploy it responsibly, with transparency and human oversight at the core.

Policy & Economy

Electric Vehicles: Future of Tomorrow; Policies Need Reshaping

Everyone today is talking about the urgency for decreasing air pollutants, the majority of which in urban cities are contributed by passenger and commercial vehicles. A ride in an EV is a most pleasant experience — jerk free, smooth and refreshing.

Challenges Associated with EVs

  • Limited mileage: EVs are not viable for long drives due to limited mileage per charge.
  • Insufficient charging stations: The lack of charging stations across cities hinders widespread adoption.
  • Higher cost: EVs are more expensive, making them inaccessible to the middle-income category.
  • Myth of reduced pollution: 46% of carbon emissions come from the EV production process vs 26% for ICE vehicles.

Critique of Delhi's EV2.0 Policy

The policy targets CNG-based vehicles, which are already non-polluting, rather than focusing on petrol and diesel vehicles. It disregards the financial burden of cab drivers who make their living from these vehicles. Imagine being asked to sell your vehicle at peanuts and buy another at triple the cost without any incremental income.

National-Level Recommendations

  • Issue guidelines to cab aggregators to not permit new non-electric vehicles rather than mandating forced conversion.
  • Install 2.5 lakh public charging stations by 2025 as planned by the Ministry of Power.
  • Extend subsidies under the FAME-II scheme for passenger vehicles.
  • Provide financial support and training to affected cab drivers and CNG service engineers.

Global Finance

Globalization of the Rupee: India's De-Dollarization Drive in a Multipolar World

India's rupee internationalisation drive is unfolding against two dramatic backdrops. The ongoing US-Israel-Iran conflict has strengthened the dollar and pushed crude prices higher — but simultaneously reinforced the strategic case for reducing dollar dependence in trade settlements. Domestically, BJP's historic win in West Bengal has strengthened the Centre's capacity to push economic and policy reforms.

Where Things Stand

The RBI introduced the Special Rupee Vostro Account (SRVA) framework in 2022. By February 2025, 123 correspondent banks from 30 countries had opened 156 such accounts. India now trades in its own currency with 24 nations. The share of foreign currency assets in India's forex reserves has declined from 93% in 2020–21 to 79.9% in 2025–26.

What's in It for India

Every percentage point reduction in dollar-dependence reduces India's exposure to US Federal Reserve policy decisions. Rupee-settled trade insulates a portion of Indian commerce from external shocks. A stronger global role for the rupee enhances the international competitiveness of Indian businesses.

Geopolitical Headwinds

De-dollarization is not a geopolitically neutral act. India has charted a cautious path — expanding rupee trade without formally endorsing a BRICS currency or directly confronting the dollar system. This balanced approach reduces the risk of diplomatic blowback from Washington while still advancing India's strategic monetary interests.

The path is promising but long. Full capital account convertibility, deep financial markets, and policy patience will determine whether the rupee graduates from a regional settlement currency to a genuine global reserve currency.

Politics & Democracy

Impact of Social Media on India's 2026 Assembly Elections

The 2026 Assembly Elections — deciding 824 legislative assembly seats across West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Assam, and Puducherry — have made social media not merely a campaign tool, but the very arena in which political battles are fought.

From Traditional Rallies to Digital Battlegrounds

Conventional campaigning still exists, but it now operates in tandem with an equally intense digital campaign running simultaneously across X, Instagram, YouTube, and WhatsApp. Narendra Modi was one of the first Indian leaders to deploy social media at scale in 2014; the 2026 elections represent the full maturation of that shift.

The Rise of Influencers

An influencer in Tamil Nadu with two million followers can shape political narratives in ways that rival legacy media outlets. Parties have actively courted content creators and regional YouTubers to amplify their messages. The influencer economy is no longer peripheral to Indian politics — it is central to it.

The Shadow Side: Misinformation and Deepfakes

With the rise of AI, the threat of deepfakes, AI-generated audio clips, and algorithmically amplified false narratives has grown sharply. In a diverse, multilingual country like India, misinformation spreads far faster than fact-checkers can counter it.

The Way Forward

Virtual campaigning is not a substitute for traditional democratic engagement, but a complement to it. The most effective campaigns integrate digital outreach with grassroots mobilisation. For citizens, the task is to engage critically — verify before sharing, and recognise that the algorithm's version of events may not be the complete picture.

Geopolitics

India's Strategic Autonomy: Leveraging Global Contradictions for National Interests

Strategic autonomy refers to a nation's ability to make independent decisions without being unduly influenced by external pressures. Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar has redefined it as a "choice of action" rather than a "choice of inaction" — emphasizing India's proactive approach to global affairs.

Historical Instances

Indira Gandhi's role in the liberation of Bangladesh in 1971, Atal Bihari Vajpayee's nuclear tests in 1998 despite international sanctions, and Dr. Manmohan Singh's Indo-US nuclear deal in 2008 against domestic opposition are all defining examples of India exercising strategic autonomy.

India's Balancing Act

India participates in the Quad while simultaneously purchasing the S-400 missile defense system from Russia despite US sanctions. India engages with the Eurasian Economic Union and strengthens ties with the UAE and Saudi Arabia — all while maintaining its neutrality on the Ukraine conflict.

Conclusion

This is a time for India to engage America, manage China, cultivate Europe, reassure Russia, bring Japan into play, draw neighbours in, extend the neighbourhood, and expand its established alliances — all while continuing to reform economically and grow faster in a democracy that is witnessing an ever more vivid expression of beliefs and traditions.
